title: Srikanth Falls in China Masters Quarterfinals After Stunning Victor Lai Upset
excerpt: Former world No. 1 Kidambi Srikanth earned his first Super 750 quarterfinal in three years but fell 16-21, 16-21 to Lee Cheuk Yiu at Shenzhen Arena.
body:
• Kidambi Srikanth lost 16-21, 16-21 to Hong Kong's Lee Cheuk Yiu in the China Masters quarterfinals at Shenzhen Arena on Friday
  • The quarterfinal appearance was Srikanth's first at BWF Super 750 level or above in three years, marking a return to elite-level competition
  • Srikanth upset Canada's Victor Lai — world No. 9 and recent World Championship bronze medallist — 21-18, 21-19 in the pre-quarterfinals
  • India's remaining hopes at the tournament rest with men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty

Kidambi Srikanth's China Masters campaign ended in the quarterfinals on Friday after the former world No. 1 fell 16-21, 16-21 to Hong Kong's Lee Cheuk Yiu at the Shenzhen Arena. The straight-games defeat concluded what had been a resurgent run for the 33-year-old at the BWF Super 750 tournament.

Despite the loss, the quarterfinal itself was a milestone. It was Srikanth's first last-eight appearance at a BWF World Tour Super 750 event or above in three years — a significant marker for a player who had struggled to compete consistently at the sport's top tier.

A Vintage Upset Against Lai

Srikanth's path to the quarterfinals was the real story of his tournament. In the pre-quarters, he produced a standout upset against Canada's Victor Lai, the world No. 9 and a recent World Championship bronze medallist, winning 21-18, 21-19.

The victory over Lai was the kind of result that had eluded Srikanth for years at this level. Before that, he had dispatched Chinese Taipei's Chi Yu-jen, ranked world No. 21, in a brisk 21-16, 21-15 opening-round victory that lasted just 35 minutes.

Lee's Dominance Continues

Against Lee Cheuk Yiu, Srikanth made an attacking start but could not consistently break through his opponent's defensive structure. Lee controlled the first game from the midpoint and closed it 21-16.

The second game was tighter. The players were level at 14-14 before Lee stepped up in the closing stages, winning seven of the last nine points to seal the match. Srikanth has now lost four consecutive matches against Lee, with his only career victory over the Hong Kong player coming at the 2018 India Open.

"It was Srikanth's first last-eight showing at a BWF World Tour Super 750 event or above in three years."

— The Bridge

India's Singles Campaign Over

Srikanth's exit means India no longer has a singles player remaining in the China Masters draw. India's women's singles challenge had already ended on Thursday when Tanvi Sharma lost 21-17, 18-21, 21-16 to Japan's Tomoka Miyazaki. Mixed doubles pair Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto were also eliminated in the second round, losing 21-18, 21-18 to Chinese Taipei's Liu Kuang-Heng and Hsu Yin-Hui.

Satwik-Chirag Carry India's Hopes

The country's remaining challenge rests with men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty. The former world No. 1 duo reached the quarterfinals after a gripping three-game win over French brothers Christo Popov and Toma Junior Popov, prevailing 21-15, 22-24, 21-9.

Satwik and Chirag were scheduled to face Denmark's Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen later on Friday for a place in the semifinals.

What It Means for Srikanth

For Srikanth, the China Masters offered evidence that he can still compete with the world's best on his day. The Lai upset and the manner of his early-round dominance suggest the veteran still has the shot-making ability and court craft that once took him to the world No. 1 ranking. The question is whether he can string together deeper runs more consistently on the World Tour circuit.
nri_angle: Srikanth remains one of India's most recognizable badminton players globally, and his resurgent form at the China Masters gives Indian fans reason for optimism.
